title: How are terminal plug-in days charged on a reefer service?
content:
## Scope

This calculation guide of **Reefer Cargo Services** covers the plug-in and monitoring fee for the days a laden reefer stands plugged in at the load terminal and at the discharge terminal.

## Rule

1. Terminal plug-in is charged per **started** calendar day that the laden reefer is plugged in.
2. At the load terminal the days run from the plug-in date to the departure date; at the discharge terminal from discharge to the delivery date (the day the laden reefer leaves the discharge terminal). At both terminals the first and the last day are counted.
3. At each terminal the tier's free days come first and are not charged; each remaining day is charged at that terminal's daily rate for the tier.
4. Each terminal stay is charged as one fee record, showing the days charged, the last plug-in day and the terminal port.
5. Plug-in may be charged only once the reefer has departed or been delivered, that is, while the service is in transit or delivered.
6. Plug-in at a transshipment port is included in the service and is not charged under this rule.

## Tier rates and free days

| Tier | Load terminal rate per day | Free days at load | Discharge terminal rate per day | Free days at discharge |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AHL Reefer Standard | 48.00 USD | 0 | 52.00 USD | 0 |
| AHL Reefer Monitored | 55.00 USD | 0 | 60.00 USD | 1 |
| AHL Reefer Cold Treatment | 60.00 USD | 1 | 65.00 USD | 1 |
| AHL Reefer Controlled Atmosphere | 70.00 USD | 1 | 75.00 USD | 1 |
| AHL Reefer Pharma GDP | 95.00 USD | 2 | 100.00 USD | 2 |
| AHL Reefer Superfreezer | 120.00 USD | 0 | 130.00 USD | 0 |

## Calculation, step by step (for each terminal stay)

1. Count the plug-in days, first and last day included.
2. Subtract the tier's free days for that terminal; if nothing remains, no day is charged (the chargeable days never go below zero).
3. Multiply the chargeable days by that terminal's daily rate for the tier.

The figures produced here are the plug-in fee before any contract-holder reduction.

## Worked example (hypothetical dates)

> **AHL Reefer Controlled Atmosphere.**
> - Load terminal: plugged in on 3 August, vessel departs on 6 August. Plug-in days: 3, 4, 5 and 6 August, which is 4 days. Less 1 free day leaves 3 chargeable days, multiplied by 70.00 USD per day, giving 210.00 USD for the load terminal stay.
> - Discharge terminal: discharged on 20 August, delivered on 21 August. Plug-in days: 2. Less 1 free day leaves 1 chargeable day, multiplied by 75.00 USD, giving 75.00 USD for the discharge terminal stay.
> - Two fee records result, one per terminal stay.

> **AHL Reefer Pharma GDP**, load terminal: plugged in on 1 September, departs on 2 September. Plug-in days: 2. The 2 free days absorb both, so no day is charged for that stay.

> **AHL Reefer Standard**, load terminal: plugged in and departed on the same day, 12 October. That single started day counts as 1 plug-in day; with 0 free days it is charged at 48.00 USD.

## Points of judgement

**Wrong reading:** "Only full 24-hour periods are charged." **Correct basis:** each started calendar day counts, and both the first and the last day of the stay are counted.

**Wrong reading:** "Free days at load that were not used carry over to the discharge terminal." **Correct basis:** free days are set separately for each terminal and are applied to that terminal's own stay.

**The vessel called at a transshipment port and the reefer was plugged in there for five days.** Transshipment plug-in is included in the service; it is not charged as a terminal stay.
